subject: biology

items.q: During exercise a person's body temperature rises above its optimum level. Why does the body respond to bring the temperature back down?
items.correct: To keep optimum conditions for enzyme action
items.misconception: To make the person feel comfortable when hot
items.why: Students meet temperature, thirst and hunger as feelings they experience, so they explain the control of these conditions in terms of how the body feels rather than in terms of what cells need. Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions; the sensations a person feels are not the reason the conditions are regulated.
items.random_wrong: To stop the internal conditions from changing

items.q: The pancreas releases a hormone that lowers a high blood glucose concentration. Which statement about this control system is correct?
items.correct: A chemical response restores the optimum level
items.misconception: A nervous response restores the optimum level
items.why: Automatic control is usually taught first using reflex examples, so students link anything automatic to nerve impulses and overlook chemical responses. These automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses, for example a chemical response coordinated by the pancreas.
items.random_wrong: A chemical response prevents the level changing

items.q: A person becomes cold and begins to shiver. Which structure is acting as the effector in this control system?
items.correct: the muscles that contract to make the body shiver
items.misconception: the receptors that detect the fall in temperature
items.why: Receptors and coordination centres are described first and are the parts students remember best, so they credit them with carrying out the response as well as with detecting and processing. Receptors detect stimuli, coordination centres receive and process information from receptors, and effectors, muscles or glands, bring about responses which restore optimum levels.
items.random_wrong: the brain that processes information from receptors

items.q: Does homeostasis hold the internal conditions of the body at exactly the same value?
items.correct: No. Internal conditions do change, and homeostasis regulates them so that they are restored to the optimum in response to internal and external changes.
items.misconception: The internal conditions of the body stay constant and do not change.
items.why: The word 'maintain', and graphs drawn as a flat line, lead students to picture a value that is held fixed rather than one that moves away from the optimum and is then brought back. Homeostasis is the regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum conditions for function in response to internal and external changes; effectors bring about responses which restore optimum levels after a change has been detected.
items.note: no MCQ covers this misconception, so no third distractor was authored for it; none invented

specSource: AQA GCSE Biology (8461) specification; section 4.5.1 Homeostasis
